column1: # Lines starting with `#` and blank lines are ignored; a field containing a comma is double-quoted.
# A rule is **confronted** on a baseline when some observation of its collector carries the fields the
# rule's `match` names and comes within one unsatisfied condition of firing it — the baseline was asked
# the rule's question and answered no. A rule no baseline confronts is quiet there for a reason that

column2: No baseline carries a Security channel. `baseline-elevated-win11` vendors one .evtx file, a LanguagePackSetup operational log, whose records agree with none of this rule's three conditions. Fabricating a Security log to give the gate something to measure is what fixtures/hosts/PROVENANCE.md forbids: a baseline is the claim that a machine like this is unremarkable, and an invented one claims nothing.
column3: A baseline carries a Security channel whose records this project is allowed to publish. fixtures/evtx/PROVENANCE.md forbids capturing from a player machine and says why: a Security record routinely carries a user name, a host name, a source IP, a SID and a command line, records cannot be redacted in place because each is checksummed within its chunk, and both the rendered-record and raw-string scans must be run before anything is vendored. So the capture has to come from a Windows 11 installation made for this purpose — throwaway local account, no network sign-in, nothing personal on it — and not from anyone real. MEASURED 2026-09-13 on one real Windows 11 machine (build 26220, elevated scan): its Security channel carried four Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog records with event id 1100, and no 1102. Those agree with this rule on provider and channel and differ on the event id, so a Security log from a machine of that kind confronts this rule at two conditions of three with no clearing having happened. The expectation this row carried before is now a measurement, on one machine.

column3: A baseline carries a System channel captured under the same conditions as the rule above, with its PROVENANCE row. MEASURED 2026-09-13 on one real Windows 11 machine (build 26220, elevated scan): across 156 record groups on its System channel, NOT ONE was written by Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog. The doubt this row carried is settled in the unhelpful direction — an ordinary System log does not appear to confront this rule, so vendoring one would not close this row and might show that nothing can. Before capturing anything, check a second machine: if that also holds no Microsoft-Windows-Eventlog record on System, the question to answer is whether this rule can be confronted at all, not which fixture to add.
